title: Lease Violation Notices on the Apartment Home Lease
content:
A violation notice (cure or quit) addresses a non-monetary breach of an Apartment Home Lease covenant.

**When it may be served.** A violation notice may be served only while the lease is active or in default, as the lease record shows. It is served for one covenant breached, one notice per covenant per service date.

**Unauthorized occupant.** A guest who stays more than the floor plan's consecutive guest nights allowed is an unauthorized occupant.

**Cure period.** The cure period is the number of days fixed for the community's state, the day of service not counted. In California only days that are not Saturdays, Sundays or California court holidays count; elsewhere calendar days count.

| State of the community | Cure period (days) |
|---|---|
| California (CA) | 3 |
| Washington (WA) | 10 |
| Colorado (CO) | 10 |
| Texas (TX) | 10 |
| Georgia (GA) | 7 |
| Arizona (AZ) | 10 |

**Effect.** A violation notice demands no money (the amount demanded is 0.00) and never changes the lease status. Damage it describes is charged at move-out under the Security Deposit Account charter, not on the lease ledger.

**Beyond the notice.** Whether an uncured violation leads to a termination action is decided by community management and counsel, not by resident services.

### Illustrations (hypothetical)

- With a guest allowance of 14 consecutive nights, a guest on the 14th consecutive night is within the allowance; on the 15th consecutive night the guest is an unauthorized occupant.
- A Georgia notice served on 2 June: the day of service is not counted, the 7 cure days are 3 through 9 June, and the cure deadline is 9 June.
- Two covenants breached and served on the same date are two notices; the same covenant cannot be the subject of two notices on one service date.
- A lease that is eviction filed or vacated is not in a status in which a violation notice may be served.
